summary_rationale: TARIL has credible high-voltage engineering qualifications, record FY26 production (33,763 MVA), strong Q2 FY27 execution (revenue +61% YoY to ₹739 Cr, ₹7,237 Cr backlog, and first nuclear-sector order from NPCIL), and operational CRGO processing via Posco-Poggenamp. However, the business remains structurally cyclical and working-capital intensive: FY26 CFO was negative ₹105 Cr, standalone working capital stayed stretched at 154 days in H1 FY27, consolidated borrowings jumped 27% in six months to ₹581 Cr, and CWIP nearly doubled to ₹267 Cr ahead of the ₹1,250 Cr Chiyada greenfield capex. Moreover, Pass 1 blind-spot forensics surfaced material governance and competitive risks omitted from the baseline: World Bank Sanctions Case No. 788 (Nov 2025 debarment notice later removed pending contested proceedings), a 2023 GETCO stop-deal sanction (later lifted), rapid departures of both external professional CEOs (3 and 6 months), sharp institutional ownership decline (DIIs 7.68% to 1.19%), and synchronized 2025–2028 industry capacity additions from Hitachi Energy, CG Power, and IPO-bound TMC Transformers.
